title: unify-flow-control-cancel-and-auth-idempotency-shims-across-sdks
author: Maya Chen
release_notes:
- Added cancellable/flow-aware streaming contexts across Python/TS/Go SDKs.
- Introduced idempotent retry shim for streaming reconnection and auth rotation.
- Ergonomic improvements: Python context-manager for stream, TS AbortSignal integration, Go context propagation + iterator helpers.
- Bumped versions: py->0.39.0, ts->2.8.0, go->v1.7.0.
description:
Background and motivation: multiple teams reported hard-to-handle streaming cancellation + token rotation races in customer integrations. This PR implements a cross-SDK pattern ("flow-cancel + idempotent-retry shim") that: 1) lets callers cancel streams deterministically (Python context manager, TS AbortSignal, Go context.Context propagation), 2) ensures streaming reconnects are safe when auth tokens rotate mid-stream (lease-based token provider + idempotency keys), and 3) improves ergonomics for common patterns (with/using semantics and docs/examples).

What this PR contains (single string):
- Commits (high level):
  * introduce flow-aware stream context managers/abstractions in py/ts/go
  * implement lease-token provider to serialize token handoff with streaming kernel
  * add idempotent-retry shim to streaming runtime client, store per-chunk resume markers
  * ergonomics: Python context manager and async iterator helpers, TS AbortSignal adapter + AsyncIterable wrapper, Go StreamIterator convenience helpers and examples
  * unit/integration tests + e2e smoke for hosted streaming with simulated token rotation
  * docs + changelogs + version bumps across the three SDKs

- Files / areas touched (high level):
  * sdk/python/redwood/streaming.py (new ContextManagedStream, StreamResumeToken)
  * sdk/python/redwood/auth/lease_provider.py (new)
  * sdk/python/tests/test_stream_cancel_token_rotation.py
  * sdk/typescript/src/stream/abort-adapter.ts (AbortSignal -> stream adapter)
  * sdk/typescript/src/stream/iterable-wrapper.ts
  * sdk/typescript/__tests__/stream-reconnect.spec.ts
  * sdk/go/stream/iterator.go (context-aware iterator)
  * sdk/go/auth/leaseprovider.go
  * shared/proto/streaming.proto (minor resume token additions)
  * docs/sdk/streaming-cancellation.md
  * examples/streaming/stream-cancel-demo (py/ts/go)

- Short code snippets (illustrative):
  * Python: with client.open_stream(prompt) as s: s.send('...')
  * TypeScript: const controller = new AbortController(); client.stream(req, {signal: controller.signal})
  * Go: ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 30*time.Second); defer cancel(); it := client.Stream(ctx, req)

Compatibility/migration notes:
- The public generation interfaces are unchanged. Streaming helpers are additive. The resume token field is optional and backward compatible in the wire proto. Consumers who currently rely on raw ws streams with custom token refresh may opt into the new lease provider or keep the existing behavior.

Testing and CI:
- Unit test coverage added across py/ts/go (~45 new tests). Integration harness simulates mid-stream token expiry and verifies reconnects resume from the last acked chunk.
- CI: initial run showed one flaky test in ts e2e (race on AbortSignal teardown). Fixed by explicit microtask drain in adapter. Final CI: pass.

Review conversation (condensed):
- Ravi: "Overall direction LGTM. A few nitty things: can we keep the resume token encoding stable and ensure proto backward compat? Also please add an explicit example for server-driven token rotation."
- Maya: "Addressed: added base64-stable encoding for resume tokens, updated proto comments, added server-rotation example and test harness."
- Elena: "TS adapter looks good; one comment on exposing AbortSignal in the public types for better discoverability."
- Maya: "Made AbortSignal export on the top level stream package and updated docs."
- Samir: "Go iterator API is clean. Suggest small ergonomics change to the Next(ctx) semantics."
- Maya: "Changed Next(ctx) to accept ctx and return (chunk, err) to align with net/http idioms; updated callers."
- Final reviewers: Ravi (approved), Elena (approved), Samir (approved).

Merge and followups:
- Merged via squash. Post-merge tasks: update the examples site, coordinate SDK release PRs (deploy artifacts), and run a short canary for dedicated infra (ENG-8502).

Notes on uniqueness: this PR combines flow-control cancellation primitives with an explicit auth lease + idempotent resume shim rather than changing the kernel. That separation is designed to keep serving runtime changes minimal while offering a safe application-level pattern for streaming resumes and token handoff.
